step_pass_probability.label: Model parameter — editable. No public dataset gives per-step control-failure rates.

attempts_per_year.label: Sample assumption — no public per-company attempt rate exists.

loss_per_success.label: Sample assumption — cost of one mailbox takeover at a ~400-person company.
loss_per_success.context: IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2026 reports far higher averages for full breaches in its (mostly large-organization) sample; they are not used here because they would overstate a single-mailbox incident.

attempts_per_year.label: Sample assumption — no public per-company attempt rate exists.

loss_per_success.label: Sample assumption — cost of one account takeover.
Average reported loss per business email compromise complaint, FBI IC3 2025: $3,046,598,558 ÷ 24,768 complaints = $123,005 (rounded).
loss_per_success.citation: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3), 2025 Internet Crime Report.
loss_per_success.caveat: Complaints reported to IC3; averages are pulled up by a few very large losses (the median is lower).

loss_per_success.label: Mean cost to recover from a ransomware attack, excluding any ransom paid: $1,700,200 (Sophos, The State of Ransomware 2026, n = 2,158).
loss_per_success.caveat: Survey mean across all organization sizes; excludes ransom payments (the median ransom paid was reported at $769,000).

context_figures.label: Global average cost of a data breach: $4.99M (IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026, released 29 July 2026; 602 organizations).
context_figures.use: Context only (shown on the Methodology page). Not used in calculations.

published_figures.citation: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3), 2025 Internet Crime Report

published_figures.metric: Loss per success (recovery cost excluding ransom)
published_figures.calculation: Mean cost to recover from a ransomware attack, excluding any ransom paid (n = 2,158)

methodology.loss_model: FAIR-style (Factor Analysis of Information Risk, Open Group standard): Annual Loss Exposure = Attempts per year × Probability of success × Loss per success
methodology.rosi_formula: ROSI (Return on Security Investment, ENISA standard) = (Risk reduction − Annual cost) / Annual cost
methodology.monte_carlo: PERT distribution with 10,000 iterations, seed 42, reporting P10 (10th percentile), P50 (median) and P90 (90th percentile).
